model: Regulated utility dividend discount (equity stream) capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

deal_analysis.status: Pending. Merger agreement signed May 2026; both shareholder votes passed September 2026; joint applications filed July 2026 with the Virginia SCC, the North Carolina and South Carolina commissions, FERC and the NRC; HSR clearance also required. Expected close H2 2027.
deal_analysis.consideration: Per Dominion share: 0.8138 NextEra shares (fixed ratio, no collar found in the 10-Q summary) plus a pro rata share of USD 360m aggregate cash (about USD 0.41 per share on 879.6m shares). Source: Q3 2026 10-Q, Proposed Merger note (D_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt lines 7078-7089).
deal_analysis.nee_price_as_of: 2026-11-13T21:00:02Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); NEE 52-week range 74.41-98.75
deal_analysis.deal_value_vs_standalone: The deal-implied value sits above all three standalone scenario values produced by this model, including the bull case. The market price sits a few percent below deal-implied value and well above standalone value: the stock is trading on the NextEra exchange ratio less a completion and timing discount, not on standalone fundamentals.
deal_analysis.implied_completion_probability_note: Illustrative only: if a broken deal sent the stock back to this model's standalone weighted value, the current price would imply a completion probability in the mid-80s percent (price - break value) / (deal value - break value). The break value is the weak input; the 52-week low of 55.85 predates or brackets the announcement and gives a similar answer.
deal_analysis.what_the_deal_value_is_not: The deal value is NextEra's MARKET price times the ratio, not an intrinsic value. NextEra has not been valued in this research folder, so nothing here says whether 0.8138 NextEra shares are worth what the market currently pays for them. A holder who keeps Dominion through closing becomes a NextEra shareholder and needs that valuation.
risks_to_completion: Virginia SCC review, with political scrutiny of data-centre cost allocation and a pre-review questionnaire sought by the Lieutenant Governor
North Carolina and South Carolina commission approvals, FERC section 203, NRC licence transfers, HSR
Conditions attached to approval (the proposal already carries USD 2.25bn of customer bill credits) that could change the economics for NextEra
Fixed ratio: the value received moves one-for-one with NextEra's share price until closing
A previously interested rival bidder ('Party A') is disclosed in the deal background; this is as much a floor under a failed deal as a risk to it
deal_analysis.interim_restrictions: Dominion may not pay dividends above USD 0.6675 per quarter without NextEra's consent, must redeem the Series C preferred if closing is after January 2027, and expects to settle outstanding at-the-market forward sales before closing.
deal_analysis.refresh_note: nee_price, implied_deal_value_per_share and the spread are a snapshot. A price-only refresh of this file's current_price does not update them; recompute from the live NextEra price.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS CAGRs are not usable: FY2020 GAAP EPS was negative (-0.57, Atlantic Coast Pipeline cancellation) and FY2022 (1.33) carried large charges, so the 3-year figure is a recovery from a depressed base and the 5-year figure is undefined. The equity CAGR is on TOTAL equity including NCI and preferred and is depressed by the 2023-2024 gas-utility divestitures.
historical_growth.notes: Free cash flow is negative in every recent year (FY2023 -3,639, FY2024 -7,180, FY2025 -7,280 before SBC), so no FCF CAGR exists; SBC (36-64m a year) is immaterial to the series. Dividend per share has been flat at 2.67 since 2022 after the 2020 reset from 3.76. The forward path is anchored on management's 5-7% operating EPS growth guidance through 2030 and the rate-base growth that the capital plan implies, not on the trailing CAGRs.

scenario_narratives.base: Standalone Dominion delivers its plan. Virginia data-centre load keeps growing, the USD 64.7bn 2026-2030 capital programme goes into rate base at the authorised 9.8% return in Virginia, the offshore wind project finishes around the end of 2027 inside the cost-sharing band, and operating EPS compounds at the midpoint of the 5-7% guidance from a 2026 result in the top half of the range. Equity issuance of USD 1.6-1.8bn a year continues and is already inside the per-share growth rate. The dividend stays at 2.67 until payout falls to 65% (2029), then grows with earnings. Growth fades to 4% in the 2030s and 3% in perpetuity.
scenario_narratives.bull: Data-centre demand runs ahead of the PJM forecast, the new 14-year minimum-demand contracts from January 2027 remove stranded-cost risk, the 2027 biennial review is constructive, offshore wind completes on budget and financing costs ease. Operating EPS grows at the top of the guided range through 2030 and the dividend starts rising a year earlier. This remains a standalone case: it does not include any merger premium.
scenario_narratives.bear: The risks specific to Dominion arrive together: an AI capital-spending pullback or cost-allocation politics slows Virginia load growth, offshore wind costs move past the USD 10.3bn sharing threshold toward the USD 13.7bn no-recovery ceiling, the Virginia commission trims returns or orders refunds in the biennial review, and higher-for-longer rates raise the cost of the USD 6-9.5bn a year of debt and the dilution from equity issuance. Per-share earnings grow 4% instead of 5-7%, the dividend is frozen until 2030, and long-run growth is 2.5%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Dominion is valued as what it is: a regulated monopoly whose shareholders receive a dividend funded by an allowed return on a growing equity base. Free cash flow is negative and will stay negative through the capital plan, so the model discounts the per-share dividend stream that the guided EPS path supports, at an 8% cost of equity, with no net-debt deduction. On that basis every standalone scenario, including the bull case, is worth less than the current share price: the market is paying roughly 19x 2026 operating earnings, which this model only reaches at a cost of equity of about 7% (see the sensitivity grid). The price is not set by standalone value. Since May 2026 it has been set by the pending all-stock merger with NextEra Energy at 0.8138 NextEra shares plus about 41 cents of cash per Dominion share; deal_analysis carries the implied value, the spread and the completion risks. The intrinsic values in this file answer 'what is Dominion worth if the merger fails'. Owning the stock today is mainly a position in NextEra at a small discount with regulatory completion risk, and NextEra itself has not been valued here.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount-rate sensitivity: the stream is long-duration; a one-point change in the cost of equity moves value by roughly 17-23%. The current price implies about 7%.

The merger: if it closes, standalone value is irrelevant and the holder receives NextEra shares at whatever they are then worth; if it fails, the price has a long way to fall toward standalone value, cushioned by a disclosed rival bidder
Per-share growth depends on the amount and price of equity issued each year; issuance at lower prices dilutes the 5-7% path
Virginia biennial review outcomes and any change to the 9.8% authorised return
Offshore wind cost recovery above USD 10.3bn and none above USD 13.7bn
Data-centre load growth and who pays for the infrastructure built to serve it
FY2025 operating EPS and the pre-announcement share price were not available in the extracted filings; the year-1 anchor is guidance and the break price is an estimate

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 55.85-72.99. NextEra price from the same endpoint at deal_analysis.nee_price_as_of.
data_sources.financials: D_Metrics.csv and core_metrics via make dcf-context; FY2025 10-K (income statement, cash flow, equity statement); Q3 2026 10-Q (balance sheet at 2026-09-30, diluted share count, Proposed Merger note).
data_sources.qualitative: D_Analysis.json dated 2026-11-15 (guidance as of the Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-30, merger timeline, capital plan, risks).

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement / Metrics.csv StockBasedComp (USD 46m, 0.28% of revenue). Already expensed inside the earnings stream (other O&M), so the forward sbc_pct_path is 0 to avoid charging it twice; house and street bases coincide.
inputs.share_count_basis: Q3 2026 10-Q weighted-average diluted shares (882.1m = 879.5m basic + 2.6m dilutive; cover page 879.57m outstanding at 2026-10-23). Held FLAT: the growth path is operating EPS growth, which is already net of the ~USD 1.6-1.8bn/yr at-the-market equity issuance that funds the capital plan. Growing the count as well would charge that dilution twice.
inputs.base_revenue_definition: The engine's 'revenue' line is EARNINGS AVAILABLE TO COMMON, not sales. FY0 = FY2025 GAAP net income attributable to Dominion Energy 2,998 less preferred dividends 44 = 2,954 (FY2025 10-K lines 11007, 11201). Year 1 is set so that earnings / 882.1m shares equals the FY2026 operating EPS judgment (base 3.60, inside the top half of the reaffirmed 3.45-3.69 range). ebitda margin 100%, D&A 0 and tax 0 because the stream is already after depreciation, interest, tax, NCI and preferred dividends. capex_pct_path is the RETENTION ratio (1 - dividend payout), so engine 'FCF' = common dividends.
inputs.last_fcf_definition: last_fcf is the FY2025 value of the stream being capitalised: common dividends paid, USD 2,278m (FY2025 10-K line 11265), NOT owner FCF. Owner FCF is structurally negative in a rate-base build-out: FY2025 operating cash flow 5,361 less plant additions 12,641 = reported_fcf -7,280 (-7,326 after SBC). FY2024 -7,180, FY2023 -3,639. That is growth capex earning an allowed return, funded by debt and equity issuance, and is not a distress signal.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The 'wacc' field is a COST OF EQUITY of 8.0%, applied to a post-interest equity stream, with net debt held at zero in the bridge (subtracting the USD 54.2bn of net debt from a dividend stream would deduct it twice). Built in USD: ~4.3% 10-year Treasury + ~0.7 beta x ~5.0% equity risk premium = ~7.8%, rounded up to 8.0% for holding-company leverage (debt/capital 53.5%, BBB-range ratings) and construction exposure. For reference Virginia Power's authorised ROE is 9.8%. The same rate is used in all three scenarios: risk is carried by the scenario paths and weights, not by per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable on this route: lease costs (USD 1.29bn of lease liabilities at FY2025) are already inside the earnings stream, and no debt-like item is deducted in the bridge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only stream. Stonepeak's 50% of the CVOW project (NCI USD 4,861m at Q3 2026; NCI earnings 267m in 9M 2026) and the USD 991m Series C preferred are excluded from earnings available to common, so nothing further is deducted in the bridge.
inputs.book_value_note: Common equity at 2026-09-30 = total equity 34,415 - NCI 4,861 - preferred 991 = USD 28,563m, about USD 32.4 per diluted share. The Metrics.csv ShareholdersEquity column is TOTAL equity including NCI and preferred.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: regulated electric utility holding company. The owner-FCF DCF does not apply -- free cash flow is negative by about USD 7bn a year while the USD 64.7bn 2026-2030 capital plan is built, and the value accrues through a regulated return on a growing equity base, not through free cash. Routed instead as a post-interest equity stream capitalised at the cost of equity (the same family as the REIT AFFO and bank routes in dcf-methods): operating EPS path x dividend payout, discounted at 8.0%, net debt zero, run through the Drivers engine. A LIVE ALL-STOCK MERGER WITH NEXTERA ENERGY IS PENDING (see deal_analysis). The dcf-methods routing table would normally weight deal-completes against deal-breaks for a live deal; by explicit instruction, and following the RWC.AX precedent, the three scenarios here are STANDALONE and the deal is carried in the separate deal_analysis block. The intrinsic values therefore describe what Dominion is worth if the merger fails, not what a holder receives if it closes. SBC is USD 46m and no shares are repurchased; the count rises through at-the-market issuance, which the EPS growth path already absorbs. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print. DATA GAP: Metrics.csv has no CapEx or FreeCashFlow from FY2020 onward and no operating EPS series; FY2023-FY2025 capex (10,211 / 12,198 / 12,641) was read from the FY2025 10-K cash flow statement and has not been backfilled. FY2025 operating EPS is not in the extracted filings (it is published in the earnings release), so FY0 is anchored on GAAP earnings and year 1 on the FY2026 operating EPS guidance.

bear.growth_rationale: FY2026 operating EPS at 3.52 (lower half of guidance), then 4% a year -- below the guided range -- fading to 2.5%.
bear.capex_pct_rationale: Dividend frozen at 2.67 for four years because slower earnings take longer to bring payout down to 65%.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon at 8.0% less 2.5% = 18.6x dividends, about 12x year-10 earnings; the 25x cap does not bind.

base.growth_rationale: Earnings per share on a fixed 882.1m count. Year 1 lands FY2026 operating EPS at 3.60 (guidance 3.45-3.69, management pointing to the top half after a 9-month 3.02). Years 2-5 take the midpoint of the 5-7% guided range through 2030; years 6-10 fade to 4% as the data-centre build-out matures.
base.capex_pct_rationale: Retention ratio = 1 - payout. Dividend held at 2.67 per share (payout 74% -> 70% -> 66%) until payout reaches 65%, then grown with earnings at a 65% payout.
base.terminal_note: Gordon on the year-10 dividend at 8.0% less 3.0% = 20.6x dividends, about 13.4x year-10 earnings. The 25x cap (about 16x earnings at a 65% payout) does not bind. 3.0% is below the 3.5% that a 35% retention at a ~10% return on equity would sustain.

bull.growth_rationale: FY2026 operating EPS at 3.66 (near the top of guidance), then the top of the 5-7% range through 2030 and a slower fade.
bull.capex_pct_rationale: Dividend flat for two years, 65% payout reached in year 3 and held.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon at 8.0% less 3.5% = 23x dividends, about 15x year-10 earnings; the 25x cap does not bind.

entry_price.method: Dividend stream and a terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate. For a regulated utility whose equity earns roughly 10% on book, a 15% hurdle entry price is necessarily a small fraction of the cost-of-equity value; read the required_return_table for the return today's price implies.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 25x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25%, above the 15% house default, because the earnings path depends on one regulator (Virginia SCC), one demand source (data centres) and one large construction project, with heavy external financing. Base 50%: regulated returns on an approved capital plan are among the more predictable earnings streams in the folder and management has reaffirmed both the year and the long-term range. Bull 25%, below the 35% default, because it needs load growth, regulatory outcomes, construction and funding costs all to break favourably. These are weights on STANDALONE outcomes; merger completion is handled in deal_analysis, not here.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
